chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Durust, from Ibn Azhinah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, what do you say regarding al-Qada' and al-Qadar?'

He (peace be upon him) replied: I say: Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, when He gathers the servants on the Day of Resurrection, will ask them about what He assigned to them, and will not ask them about what was predestined for them.

key_terms.عَمَّا عَهِدَ إِلَيْهِمْ: Regarding what was assigned/entrusted to them
key_terms.عَمَّا قَضَى عَلَيْهِمْ: Regarding what was decreed for them

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between al-Qada and al-Qadar according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the theological distinction between *al-Qada'* (divine decree/inevitability) and *al-'Ahad* (explicit commandment), asserting that accountability on the Day of Judgment is based on what was entrusted to human free will rather than what was predestined. This supports the Shia doctrine of *Adl* (Divine Justice), emphasizing that God does not punish for what He compelled, but only for what He commanded humans to choose. The hadith underscores the principle that divine testing is limited to the scope of human agency, reinforcing the balance between predestination and free will.
